newsitem.title: USA: U.S. natgas stocks seen up 5-15 bcf in weekly AGAs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. natgas stocks seen up 5-15 bcf in weekly AGAs.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to rise by five to 15 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said this week.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations ranged from a draw of 20 bcf to a build of 30 bcf for the week ended April 4.

"It wouldn't surprise me if there was a build. The economics were certainly there for storage buying," said one Houston-based trader, referring to the 40-cent spread between cash and winter futures prices.
Traders said overall degree-day data indicated last week was a bit warmer than the prior week when stocks fell by just one bcf, well-below expectations in the 30-40 bcf range.

In last report, overall stocks were still 257 bcf, or 45 percent, above year-ago. Eastern storage last week climbed to 196 bcf over year-ago, or more than double 1996 levels. The four week average draw is 39 bcf.

For the same week last year, total inventories dropped by 15 bcf, meaning a build today in the expected range would boost the overall surplus to 1996 to about 280 bcf. Eastern storage fell by eight bcf last year, while producing stocks dropped by six bcf and western stocks by one bcf.
